introduce.name: introduce
introduce.title: What Is a Relocation Chart
introduce.label: INTRODUCTION
introduce.description: A relocation chart answers a precise question: if I keep the same birth date and clock time but imagine I was born in another city, how does my chart change? The relocation chart keeps planetary longitudes the same—Sun, Moon, and planets stay in the same zodiac signs and degrees—because the moment in time is unchanged. What does change in a relocation chart are the angles (Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, IC in a full wheel) and therefore the house system: whole-sign houses rotate with the new Ascendant. Our free relocation chart calculator shows your birth-location Ascendant side by side with the relocated Ascendant, and lists every planet with natal house versus relocated house. Run it once per candidate city before a move, a long trip, or a digital-nomad stint. To compare several places on one map, use Compare Cities after you generate your astrocartography map. The relocation chart is different from astrocartography: the map shows planetary lines worldwide; the relocation chart shows one alternate birthplace for the same instant. Use both together—the relocation chart for how the whole wheel reorganizes, astrocartography for geographic emphasis.

items.title: Why the Relocation Chart Matters
items.description: Most people discover the relocation chart when they plan to leave home. The relocation chart highlights which life topics gain angular emphasis after relocation—career angles, relationship angles, roots and family—because houses are tied to those themes. A relocation chart does not replace legal or financial advice, but it is a structured way to ask how your chart might feel in Paris versus Tokyo versus your hometown. Our relocation chart calculator uses the same astronomical approach as our birth tools: geocentric longitudes and a clear whole-sign house model so the relocation chart stays easy to read.

items.title: Relocation Chart vs Astrocartography Map
items.description: Astrocartography draws where each planet’s lines run on Earth. A relocation chart instead fixes one new spot and redraws the wheel for that spot. If you already love maps, run astrocartography next; if you want a table and angles for one destination, the relocation chart is faster. Many serious students keep both: relocation chart for the snapshot, astrocartography for the route. This page’s relocation chart calculator links you to the map with one click after you calculate.

items.title: How We Build Your Relocation Chart
items.description: You enter birth data and a relocation city. We convert your birth clock time to UTC, then compute the Ascendant at your birth coordinates and again at the relocation coordinates. Planets are evaluated at that same UTC instant. Houses follow whole signs from each Ascendant, which is standard for a readable relocation chart on the web. The relocation chart output shows planet sign and degree once, with two house columns—natal and relocated—so you instantly see what moved.

faq.name: faq
faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Relocation Chart Calculator — Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about the relocation chart and how this calculator works.

items.title: What is a relocation chart?
items.description: A relocation chart keeps your birth moment fixed in time but changes the place on Earth used to calculate angles and houses. Planetary signs and degrees stay the same; the wheel’s orientation changes. Our calculator shows that shift with two Ascendants and two house columns.

items.title: Is this relocation chart calculator free?
items.description: Yes. You can run the relocation chart as many times as you want without an account. Premium AI readings elsewhere on the site use credits; the relocation chart data itself is free.

items.title: Does a relocation chart change my planets?
items.description: No. In this relocation chart model, geocentric ecliptic longitudes are unchanged. Only angles and derived houses change, which is standard for relocation work.

items.title: How is this different from astrocartography?
items.description: Astrocartography maps many locations at once via lines. A relocation chart focuses on one chosen city and shows the reorganized houses. They answer different questions; use both for a full picture.

items.title: What house system does the relocation chart use?
items.description: We use whole-sign houses from the Ascendant at each location. It is readable and widely used for relocation-style comparisons online.

items.title: Does the relocation chart show Midheaven (MC)?
items.description: Yes. Results include Midheaven at birth and at the relocation city, alongside both Ascendants. MC highlights career and public-life angles; pair it with the house table to see which planets land on angular houses after you move.

items.title: How do I read my relocation chart results?
items.description: Start with the four angles (ASC and MC at birth vs relocation). Then scan the reading highlights: biggest house shifts, planets within 3° of an angle, and life houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th). Finally use the full planet table—natal house is your baseline, relocated house shows what changes in the new city.

items.title: Can I compare two cities in one relocation chart?
items.description: No. Each run is for one relocation city. To compare several places on one map, generate your astrocartography chart and use Compare Cities (up to four). Run this calculator separately for each finalist.

items.title: Is my birth data stored?
items.description: Calculations are processed on our servers when you submit the form. We use the data to return your relocation chart for that session. See our privacy policy for retention details.

methodology.label: METHODOLOGY
methodology.title: How We Calculate Your Relocation Chart
methodology.description: Relocation results use the method explained below.

items.title: Calculation engine
items.description: Planetary longitudes and angles use the open-source astronomy-engine library (linked above): geocentric tropical ecliptic positions—the same core math family used across AstroCarto chart calculators on this site.

items.title: Same birth moment, new coordinates
items.description: Your local birth date, time, and timezone convert to one UTC instant. That instant is fixed. We compute the Ascendant and Midheaven (MC) at your birth latitude/longitude, then again at the relocation latitude/longitude. Planetary signs and degrees do not change; only angles and derived houses do.

items.title: Whole-sign houses
items.description: Houses follow whole signs from each location’s Ascendant: the rising sign is the entire 1st house, the next sign is the 2nd, and so on. Natal and relocated house columns in the table use this model for a clear before-and-after comparison.

items.title: Reading highlights
items.description: After calculation, the tool surfaces biggest house shifts, planets within 3° of the Ascendant or MC at each location, and occupants of life houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th). These are interpretive aids—not predictions—and pair with the full planet table.

items.title: Where processing runs
items.description: When you submit the form, the browser calls /api/calculate-relocation-chart. The server returns angles, houses, and reading highlights as JSON. Birth and relocation locations are used only to perform that calculation for your session.

methodology.disclaimer: Astrology content on this page is for general information and exploration only. It is not medical, financial, legal, or other professional advice, and it does not guarantee outcomes. Use your own judgment for important decisions.
